Readiness

The correction is a substantial improvement and is ready for another user design review. It is not yet ready for web acceptance: the shared keyboard reproducibly loses the first character after Select all in the exercised inline Name flow. The counter-inheritance defect is fixed in the final web build. Compact token controls, useful counter workflows, default utility capacity, mana spending and reset/restore completion are materially better.

This is a bounded retest of priority failures, not a new claim of full 50-row parity. The earlier 2.6/5 remains the historical first-pass score. No aggregate replacement score is calculated from this smaller follow-up. Source-only gaps and native limits remain open. No source fixes, builds, tests, installs, signing or publication were performed by this reviewer.

Remaining Issues

Q01 — P1 — R + C — Web keyboard loses the initial character after Select all.

c05 c06 c07

Repro at1133×744: Player2 Treasure → expand → Name; Select all → q → a. The first key visibly yields q; the next key yields a instead of qa. Both the actual inline field and shared keyboard show the replacement. Repeated using accessibility-targeted clicks and actual pointer coordinates with a fresh state observation between actions: Select all(174,251), q(1077,160), a(1077,117). Same result. Earlier longer q/a/left/s sequences also lost text (c05,c06). c07 captures the isolated result; the step observations establish q→a. Subsequent characters sometimes append normally, so this is scoped to the initial focus/selection transition, not every keypress. Tapaway commits the shortened value.

Impact: routine rename/text input cannot be trusted on this supported web target. This blocks web acceptance despite useful inline UI restoration. Native behavior is not independently retested.

Plausible mechanism, not a fully proven root cause: player_keyboard.dart:604–624 omits selectAllOnFocus on its single-line EditableText preview; _replace calls _focusDraft before insertion at312–327. Installed Flutter defaults select-all-on-focus true on web/desktop and false on mobile, and can reselect on focus regain (SDK editable_text.dart:2106–2117,4752–4788). This matches the platform distinction. No fix made.

Q02 — P2 — C/U — Inline P/T keyboard lacks variable-stat characters.

tablet_token_card.dart:716–720 requests numeric:true; player_keyboard.dart:530–534,636–663 supplies digits/minus/slash without '*' or '+' or an ABC/symbol switch. Touchscreen inline entry of */* or1+*/1+* therefore has no key path. Detailed editor, hardware or paste remain workarounds; storage/calculation of variable P/T is not claimed absent. This was source-reviewed, not runtime exercised in the bounded pass.

Q03 — P2 — C/U — Utility history still records requested rather than effective clamped change.

The corrected mana route passed. Separate utility route board_service.dart:1118–1139 retains raw delta/label before clamping. Visual Judgment

The board now looks and behaves much closer to the deliberate original token object: compact icon actions, status counts, counter pills, modified-P/T emphasis and compact ability symbols coexist in the lane. c02 versus original47/48 makes the change concrete. Default utilities are visible in both inspected mini orientations, instead of occupying an unusably short scroller. Portrait action rows wrap to two lines and remain dense; physical touch and text scaling must still be checked. Large detailed dialogs still contain unused space, but their operations are focused and ordinary actions no longer require them. Further geometry refinement is a design iteration, not a mandate to shrink controls or force FABs.

Four-player token-side choice remains the earlier D01 open consistency question. Two-player local-left is correct in c09. No new lane-side failure is asserted. Repeated idle-board player naming was removed; captured player/token context remains correctly present in editors.
